comp_disc_analysis.notes:
[chunk 1/3] This is a DEF 14A proxy filing. The text is primarily boilerplate director bios and governance disclosures. Three SIFI-material signals were identified:

1. HIGHEST PRIORITY: Jeffrey Bezos (Amazon Executive Chair) co-founded and serves as co-CEO of "Project Prometheus," an AI company, as of November 2025 — creating a direct governance/competitive conflict with Amazon's own AI investments and AWS. This is a circularity/governance risk that should be flagged for further investigation. The filing does not disclose what Project Prometheus does, who backs it, or whether Amazon has any commercial relationship with it.

2. Director Andrew Ng has an Amazon commercial relationship with his company DeepLearning.AI (Amazon pays DeepLearning.AI). Disclosed as immaterial by the board but creates a related-party dynamic worth tracking.

3. Director Wendell Weeks is CEO/Chairman of Corning, which Amazon pays in the ordinary course. Also disclosed as immaterial. Corning is a potential data center materials supplier (fiber, specialty glass).

The filing does not name any new AI lab investments, capex commitments, SPVs, or major customer/supplier concentration risks beyond these director independence items.
[chunk 2/3] This is a DEF 14A (proxy statement) for Amazon FY2025. The filing is primarily governance/compensation boilerplate with no SIFI-material named counterparty relationships, investments in AI labs, SPVs, or revenue roundtripping disclosed directly. The only SIFI-material signal surfaced is in Item 5 (a shareholder proposal on data center climate impact), which cites a reported ~$150B / 15-year data center capex figure sourced from Bloomberg and flags a near-term energy execution gap (nuclear SMRs not operational until early 2030s). This figure is attributed to external reporting cited by a shareholder proponent, not directly confirmed by Amazon management in the filing — noted for verification. No AI lab investments, off-balance-sheet entities, customer/supplier concentration disclosures, or circular dependency relationships were identified in this section. Director compensation is standard RSU grants with no related-party angles. EY audit relationship (since 1996) and $59.3M total fees are noted but not SIFI-material.
[chunk 3/3] Key SIFI-material findings from AMZN DEF 14A (2026-04-09):

1. RELATED-PARTY / CONFLICT-OF-INTEREST: Jeff Bezos (Executive Chair of Amazon) is co-CEO of Project Prometheus, an AI startup he co-founded (named in shareholder proposal Item 7). This creates potential circularity — Amazon could become a compute customer or partner of a Bezos-controlled AI lab. Severity elevated to 3 given Bezos's dual role and Amazon's historical pattern of related-party deals.

2. RELATED-PARTY TRANSACTION: $2.7B satellite launch agreement with Blue Origin (Bezos-owned), disclosed in the shareholder proposal. This is a named, quantified related-party capex commitment surfaced in a governance challenge, not routine boilerplate.

3. CAPEX ROI GAP / COST OPACITY: Amazon does not separately disclose the incremental cost of its climate commitments vs. lowest-cost power alternatives. 700+ energy projects, 40GW capacity, 12 planned SMRs (partnered with X-energy and Energy Northwest), plus Entergy's $300M grid campaign — significant undisclosed incremental capex embedded in sustainability program.

4. Project Prometheus classified as ailab (private:true) per rules, as it is described as an AI startup where Bezos is co-CEO. Known backers: Jeff Bezos.

5. AWS generates >50% of Amazon operating income (stated in shareholder proposal) — material for concentration analysis but not separately extracted as no new counter-party named.

related_party.notes: [chunk 1/1] This DEF 14A related-party section is relatively sparse on SIFI-material structures. The dominant signal is the $7.4B satellite launch services contract (2022–2028), of which ~$2.7B is directed to Blue Origin — a company owned by Amazon's Executive Chair Jeff Bezos. In 2025 alone, ~$1.8B was estimated paid to Blue Origin. This is a material related-party supplier concentration with a single-source dependency risk for Amazon's Project Kuiper satellite program. No SPVs, VIEs, AI lab investments, or off-balance-sheet structures are disclosed in this section. Employee family compensation disclosures (Olsavsky family members) are below SIFI materiality threshold. Washington Post transactions ($840K advertising, $1.9M digital content, $800K data licensing) are immaterial. No AI lab investments, hyperscaler compute agreements, or circular dependency structures are present in this filing section.
